fields.AN_Notes: Prompts (GenderPair pair sets with instruction and requirement) are the research instrument; no named prompting technique is applied, robustness is tested across prompt structures. Bias axes: gender across three groups, with transgender and non-binary identities (Group 3) as own analysis category, hence Sexual_Orientation_Identity for gender identity alongside Gender; race, age, nationality and religion appear only in the outlook. Harm types: stereotyping measured via biased descriptors and stereotype benchmarks, toxicity measured per gender group; Regard sentiment differences are a tone measure and are not coded as Disparate_Performance; erasure of non-binary people is only cited from Ovalle et al. Mitigation: counterfactual data augmentation builds a debiasing dataset (Pre_Processing) and LoRA fine-tuning (In_Training), evaluated in the work's own experiments with bias reduction on GenderPair, Winoqueer, BOLD and StereoSet and GLUE/MMLU performance checks. Task None: general LLM benchmark without an application task. The ethical statement notes the work is grounded in Western conceptions of gender. Theory reference No: the sex/gender distinction and NIST criteria are definitional and normative sources, not a theory framing the analysis.

fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual policy paper proposing Feminist AI as a framework. Harm type: the binary gender norm as default that excludes non-binary people (Exclusionary_Norms); stereotyping appears only as a measure to be established, the masculinist understanding of intelligence is cited. Mitigation: testing training data for diversity measures and MIRA's synthetic-data training (Pre_Processing), diverse teams, stakeholder engagement, legislation advocacy and maintenance cycles (Organisational_Process). Status Demonstrated is limited to the MIRA practice example, which is described as implemented without a reported evaluation result; the other measures are proposed. Other_Task: medical diagnostics in the MIRA health-tech example. Gender understanding: patriarchy as a power structure held by men (Social_Construct) and non-binary individuals as a category of the work's own design principle (Non_Binary_Inclusive); gender is not defined in a sentence of its own. fields.AN_Notes: Introductory article of a special issue that synthesises key risks and governance challenges of generative AI and proposes a governance framework (Table 2). Bias axes None: race, ethnicity and gender appear only in an enumeration of protected characteristics; inequality is discussed in terms of digital divide, income disparities and Big Tech power without an axis the work analyses. Harm types are coded from the work's own risk and challenge synthesis (data training and validation risks, bias amplification), with supporting citations: underperformance for underrepresented demographics (Disparate_Performance) and generated media that reinforce stereotypes (Stereotyping); discrimination is named without an allocation or decision about persons and is not coded. Mitigation: diverse and representative datasets and data curation (Pre_Processing), diverse teams, stakeholder engagement, red teaming, impact assessment, internal and independent audits, standards and certification (Organisational_Process); generic detection during training and deployment does not justify further technical stages. All measures are recommendations (Proposed). Other_Task: public policymaking and urban governance (city brains with an LLM for anticipatory governance) and call-centre customer service, as summarised from the special-issue articles. Bias is not defined; the data-driven understanding is recognisable from the risk section. Gender is not an object. Theories named (complex adaptive systems, multiple streams framework, polycentric governance) frame governance, not gender or bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Normative standard-setting instrument with values, principles and eleven policy areas. Bias axes coded where the instrument develops an axis in its own policy argument: gender (dedicated Policy Area 6 on gender gaps and gender stereotyping), language and culture (Policy Area 7, endangered languages and dialects under NLP), socioeconomic status (poverty gap and digital divide in ethical impact assessment), Other_Axis for place of residence and country development status (equity between rural and urban areas, LMICs, LDCs, LLDCs and SIDS). The long lists of protected grounds (race, colour, descent, religion, disability and others) are enumerations and are not coded. Harm types: stereotyping in AI outcomes and data, gender stereotyping (Stereotyping); disappearance of endangered languages and local dialects (Erasure). Discrimination is named without classification into direct or indirect and without a specific allocation case, so neither discrimination code is assigned. Mitigation: diverse training datasets, gold-standard datasets and disaggregated data annotation (Pre_Processing); ethical impact assessment, AI ethics officers, oversight, audit, certification, diverse development teams (Organisational_Process); all as recommendations (Proposed). Other_Task: governance of AI use across sectors, including health diagnosis and treatment, judiciary and public services. Gender is not defined; the analysis addresses girls and women relative to men (Binary_Categorical). Bias is not defined; the understanding follows from the human-rights and non-discrimination frame. Theory reference No: international human rights law is a legal-normative basis, not a named theory framing gender or bias. Publication type admitted as policy document, see report.
